purpose: Repair real advice button availability and advice scoring/formatting for legal owner Judgment conversions while retaining default engine AI and replay behavior.
changes: RefreshPlayAdvice notifies the bound RelayCommand after refreshing availability and withdrawing stale advice.
The original three-argument SimpleAiBrain constructor remains and delegates with Judgment material support disabled. A separate four-argument overload enables it only for standalone advice.
Three scoring lookups append the owner's visible Judgment materials only when enabled; original default zones, order, policies and deterministic random sequence are retained.
PlayAdvisor uses the enabled independent brain and includes own Judgment material in both printed-face and effective-kind descriptions.
Regression branches extend retained Core LastZone conversion, WPF regional conversion and loaded modal-focus checks. No new registration or routine filter is added.

assertions: Policies 1, 2 and 3 preserve identical ordinary selected actions and complete thought candidate scores/reasons with Judgment support enabled versus the default brain.
Each policy retains a forced exact native Judgment Slash candidate and evaluates the complete unchanged legal action set.
The full Core state comparison includes four private player views, resolution frames, movements, facts, accepted commands and card-zone diagnostics.
The same loaded WPF button transitions setup-disabled to play-enabled, activates actual guidance, then setup-disabled with stale advice cleared, and play-enabled again on cancel.

The WPF Judgment fixture keeps all 9 actions for actual button execution. A separate Recommend invocation with the exact single legal native action forces printed Lightning suit/rank and effective Slash formatting; it does not replace the real UI action set.

Closing advice preserves four views, engine identity/revision, accepted-command and movement counts, all legal actions, exact selection text and target. The original real Judgment payment/completion assertions continue and pass.
